llm.summary: The AI complex is now repricing on multiples, not fundamentals: Applied Materials delivered a beat-and-raise with semiconductor systems growth above 40% and still gapped -6.4%, while Cisco raised its AI order outlook to $9B and fell 5%. That is the single most important tell of the week — good news is no longer paid for in AI infrastructure, which means the de-rating is about discount rates, governance and capex-digestion fear rather than demand. Jensen Huang's resignation has metastasized from a corporate event into a Washington process story (Lutnick testifying, bipartisan probes, Bessent slamming 'leakage'), which converts a scandal into durable export-control risk and a durable subsidy for domestic fabs. Macro is the other jaw of the vise: PPI at 6.5% annual is the hottest in nearly four years, the 10-year sits near 5.11%, the 2-year added 30bp in a week, BofA has added a January 2027 hike, and Treasuries just had their worst week since 'liberation day.' Real yields broke hard assets — gold touched a 13-month low near $3,850 before rebounding above $3,900, bitcoin lost $70,000. Yet the index logged its best week in months and European equities sit near records, confirming this is a rotation, not a liquidation: Health Care 96, Staples 91, Financials 79, Materials 79 versus Technology -67, with Value leading Growth by 114. Housing is the clear casualty — existing home sales at the lowest since 2010 with prices at all-time highs, a pure affordability lock-up. Neocloud credit is the stress point to watch: Nscale disclosed $5.5B of debt, a widening loss and the need for more financing ahead of its IPO, and CoreWeave gapped -11%.

market_thesis.short_term: Dispersion, not drawdown. The index held up and logged its best week in months while the AI leadership complex de-rated — capital is rotating into Health Care, Staples, Financials, Materials and Real Estate rather than into cash. The binding short-term variable is the long end: with PPI at 6.5% y/y, the 10-year near 5.11% and a January hike now in forecasts, any asset priced on duration (semis, neoclouds, gold, bitcoin, homebuilding, REITs) stays under pressure regardless of its earnings. The AMAT/CSCO reaction is the trade signal of the week: when a 40%+ systems growth print and a raised $9B AI backlog both get sold, positioning — not fundamentals — is clearing. Expect continued churn with a floor, because Technology outflows improved from -78 to -67 and the Value-Growth spread narrowed from 121 to 114, hinting the panic leg of the rotation is maturing.
market_thesis.medium_term: Reflation (33.7, +11.1) and Stagflation (33.1, +13.1) are tied with Goldilocks collapsing to 16.7 — a Fed hiking into an economy that is not breaking but whose consumer is locked out of housing. That means higher-for-longer nominal yields, a firm dollar, sustained multiple compression on narrative assets, and continued leadership from cash-generative value, insurance (investment income tailwind), healthcare distribution and managed care. Inside AI the fault line is now credit: Nscale's $5.5B debt and financing need, CoreWeave's -11% gap, and the wobbling Anthropic IPO book say the marginal dollar for GPU buildouts is getting expensive, which slows orders two to three quarters after it slows financing even as end-demand (AMAT, CSCO, TSMC) stays strong. Export-control legislation following the Nvidia case is the mechanism that turns the scandal into a permanent earnings impairment for China-exposed semis and a permanent subsidy for US semicap and reshoring. Oil swinging to surplus on rebounding Gulf and Russian supply is the one genuine disinflationary offset and a direct margin tailwind for airlines and freight.
market_thesis.long_term: The constraints on AI are electrons, permits, political consent and capital access, and the economics accrue to owners of generation, turbines, grid hardware, fabs and transition metals rather than to owners of the story — Meta funding seven gas plants for a single data center and Modi pitching nuclear for data-center load are the template. The Huang episode makes explicit that a trillion-dollar capital cycle was partly collateralized by one person's credibility; institutionalizing it means a slower, more contested, more expensive buildout and a permanently higher risk premium on key-man AI equities. Agentic commerce (ChatGPT Wallet buying on behalf of users) is the start of a decade-long re-plumbing of payments, advertising and e-commerce where intent is captured upstream of the merchant and the brand. For households, affordability is the organizing variable: 5%+ mortgages, 6.5% producer inflation, home sales at 2010 lows and emerging-market consumers levering up all entrench value retail, generics, distribution, insurance and essential services over undifferentiated discretionary.

short_term: Households are frozen out of housing — existing home sales at the lowest since 2010 with prices at all-time highs — so they are redirecting shelter dollars into staying put: repair, remodel, roof decks, appliances, and renting longer.

Investors are paying for cash flow today over narrative tomorrow: they sold AMAT after a beat-and-raise and CSCO after a raised AI outlook, while bidding Health Care (96), Staples (91) and Financials (79).

Savers are rediscovering yield as an asset class — I Bonds at 5.51%, 5%+ Treasuries, rising 401(k) limits — which structurally competes with equity risk premia and with gold and bitcoin as stores of value.
Risk appetite is migrating geographically rather than disappearing: European equities near record highs and small-cap flows turning positive while US mega-cap tech de-rates.
Consumers are trading down and leveraging up — Costco, Dollar General, Dollar Tree and Ollie's attention is high while Barron's flags emerging-market consumer spending now coming with big debt.
Travel and experiences spending is holding: hotel share prices surged into Q4 and travel-health demand is growing, even as goods demand softens.
long_term: Delegation of purchasing to agents: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents transact, shifting consumer effort from searching and comparing to approving — this reprices attention, loyalty and merchant acquisition over a decade.

Security and status are being bought through tangible, verifiable things — trading cards now a $2B market, gold accumulation despite real-yield pain, physical infrastructure ownership — as trust in narrative assets erodes.

Energy is becoming a consumer-visible cost and a political object; rising public search for 'ai data center water usage' and 'ai data center near me' signals local consent becomes a gating factor on the AI buildout.
Housing demand is being converted into renovation, multi-generational living and storage demand rather than transactions, a durable shift in where shelter dollars land.
Health is shifting from episodic treatment to continuous monitoring and metabolic management — sustained GLP-1 attention and CGM adoption reframe healthcare as a subscription on healthspan.
Workers and firms are reorganizing around productivity-per-head rather than headcount, with HR, compliance and governance re-emerging as the bottleneck in AI adoption.
